reviews.summary: The core loop is functionally solid and the on-device privacy posture is genuinely good, but the build is blind at exactly the points most likely to fail a real tester: AI calls, image decode, and storage all fail only into a transient toast with nothing captured, and there is no quality telemetry section in the spec to close that gap. Data integrity is soft in two places (the items-released stat disagrees with its own analytics definition, and a completed zone stays "done" after its after-photo is deleted), and unvalidated AI JSON can crash the zone screen on reopen. On usability and visualization, the single biggest motivational payoff, seeing the before and after side by side, is never actually rendered, and the prototype ships with essentially no accessibility affordances even though the spec commits to a screen-reader-complete loop.
reviews.top_priority: Capture quality and health telemetry for the failure-prone AI, image, and storage paths, and validate AI JSON before it renders. Today every failure in the loop is invisible to the team and one malformed AI reply can white-screen the zone.

findings.title: No quality or health telemetry; every failure dies in a toast
findings.observation: callAI surfaces errors only through toast() (app-review.js SortPlanBlock line 422, CoachBlock line 500), compress rejects decode failures into a toast (line 385), and LS.set warns 'Storage full' via toast (line 125) with the IDB-unavailable in-memory fallback announced once at boot (line 581). None of these are recorded. The spec's Analytics & Instrumentation event taxonomy (spec.json ~line 1636 onward) is entirely happy-path: app_install through audit_action, with no failure, timeout, parse, decode, or crash events. The team cannot see AI success rate, why a Sort Plan failed, or how often storage fell back to session-only.
findings.recommendation: Add a privacy-respecting quality-telemetry layer alongside the product events. Wrap callAI, compress, and the storage layer so each failure emits an enum-and-count-only event (no photo, no free text, no home or room name). Suggested events: ai_call_failed{capability, reason: no_endpoint|timeout|http_error|empty_reply|parse_failed|truncated}, ai_json_repaired{capability}, photo_decode_failed{reason}, storage_fallback_engaged, app_error{screen}. Keep the same restraint the spec already applies to product analytics.
findings.spec_change: Add a new subsection 'Quality & Health Telemetry' to the Analytics & Instrumentation section (after the Event taxonomy table, spec.json ~line 1707) with its own table of the failure events above, each row stating When it fires / Enum-only properties / What it protects, and a note that these carry no photo, name, or user text, exactly matching the existing Privacy stance callout.

findings.title: Items-released stat over-counts; code disagrees with the spec definition
findings.observation: zoneStats() computes items as (p.out.d)+(p.out.t)+(p.out.r), i.e. donated plus discarded plus RELOCATED (app-review.js line 243), and the dashboard labels it 'items released' (line 296). But the analytics event zone_completed defines items_released as 'the donate plus discard tally' (spec.json ~line 1678) and the Success Metrics / share-card hook use the same donate-plus-discard definition (~line 1750). Relocated items stay inside the home, so counting them inflates the headline motivational and share stat, and the Part III correction row actually says the opposite (that the stat OMITS relocate, ~line 2165), which is now stale versus this build.
findings.recommendation: Pick one definition and enforce it in one place. Recommended: items released = donate + discard only (matches 'released from the home' and the analytics event); show relocated as a separate 'relocated within home' count if desired. Fix zoneStats to exclude p.out.r, and make the on-device stat, the zone_completed.items_released property, and the future share card read from the same helper.
findings.spec_change: Correct the Part III 'Corrections and defects' row 'Items-released stat omits relocate' (spec.json ~line 2165) to read that the current build INCLUDES relocate and over-counts, and add a definitional line to the Success Metrics 'Items released' row (~line 1750) fixing the canonical formula as donate + discard, with relocate tracked separately.

findings.title: Deleting the after photo leaves the zone marked done
findings.observation: Completion requires all six steps plus an after photo (StepPanel line 473; auto-complete in PhotoBlock line 387). But the photo-delete path (PhotoBlock paint, line 381) runs delPhoto, splice, saveProg, paint and never recomputes p.done. So a tester who completes a zone and later deletes the after photo keeps p.done=true: the zone still counts in zoneStats zr ('zones reset'), still shows a green 'Done' pill and a filled room ring, and the AuditBlock stays visible, even though its evidence is gone. The dashboard now reports a reset that has no after photo.
findings.recommendation: Recompute completion on every photo mutation: after delete/splice set p.done = p.steps.every(Boolean) && p.ap.length>0, and if it flips to false clear p.audit. Add this as a data-integrity acceptance test (complete a zone, delete the after photo, confirm it leaves the reset count and the audit disappears).
findings.spec_change: Add an acceptance-criteria bullet under Part III 'Functional' (spec.json ~line 2453): 'Deleting the last after photo un-completes the zone; reset counts and stats always reflect present evidence.' and add a Part III corrections row 'Completion not recomputed on photo delete'.

findings.title: Unvalidated AI JSON can white-screen the zone on reopen
findings.observation: AI output is rendered raw. SortPlanBlock shows `Clutter ${a.clutter_score||'?'}/5` and iterates a.review.forEach (lines 407-411); CoachBlock shows `${a.score}/5` and iterates a.wins/a.remaining (lines 489-492). Scores are never clamped, so a model reply of score 9 or clutter 0 renders literally. Worse, if review/hazards/wins/remaining come back as a non-array (a string survives the tolerant repairParse), the .forEach or .length access throws. On the first request that error is caught into a toast, but p.aiA/p.ai is saved first (lines 421, 499), so the next time the zone is opened render() runs during ZoneScreen construction OUTSIDE any try/catch and the whole zone screen fails to render.
findings.recommendation: Add a validate-and-coerce step before caching any AI object: clamp score and clutter_score to 1-5 integers, coerce belongs/review/hazards/wins/remaining to arrays (default []), drop malformed review entries, and wrap the app in a top-level error boundary so a bad cached object degrades to the static plan instead of a blank screen. Emit ai_json_invalid telemetry when coercion fires.
findings.spec_change: Promote the P1 item 'Runtime validation of AI JSON (clamp the score and clutter values, default the arrays)' (spec.json ~line 2427) into the Part III Acceptance Criteria quality gates as a hard gate, and add 'top-level error boundary; a malformed cached AI reply never blanks a screen' to that same list (~line 2470).

findings.title: The before/after payoff is never actually shown, and time invested is an estimate
findings.observation: The whole promise is 'see the change you could not un-see', yet before and after live in two separate PhotoBlock galleries (ZoneScreen lines 357 and 366) and are never juxtaposed. There is no diptych or compare slider anywhere in the runner, even though the diptych is listed as a signature component (spec.json ~line 585) and the share card depends on it. Separately, the 'time invested' dashboard stat is not measured time at all: zoneStats derives it as (steps done / 6) x sum of the zone's minute budget (line 243), so it is an estimate presented as a fact.
findings.recommendation: Add a simple before/after compare to the Zone Runner and the Coach's Review (paired thumbnails or a slider) as the beta's one high-value visualization; it is also the exact asset the share card reuses later. Relabel the dashboard number to 'estimated time' OR measure real session duration (open-to-complete), which doubles as a useful data-collection signal for how long a real zone takes.
findings.spec_change: Add a Build-Ready Feature Backlog row (spec.json ~line 2319) 'Before/after compare in the runner and coach review' marked MUST or NICE, and add a Success Metrics / telemetry note distinguishing estimated budget time from a new optional session_duration signal; correct the Dashboard capability description that implies the change is visible.

findings.title: Prototype ships with no accessibility affordances despite a spec commitment
findings.observation: The spec's Accessibility section commits to completing a full zone loop with a screen reader and to meaning never resting on color (spec.json ~line 1352 onward), but this reference build has none of it. Substep toggles are plain buttons with a checkmark span and no role or aria-checked (StepPanel line 453); step headers have no aria-expanded (line 432); photo thumbnails are non-focusable divs with a background-image and no label or alt (PhotoBlock line 381); the settings and back controls are glyph-only buttons '⚙' and '‹' with no accessible name (TopBar line 574, Dashboard line 294); the toast has no aria-live so nothing is announced (line 238); and zone-dots and the step spine encode state by color alone (lines 311, 329).
findings.recommendation: Even in the web prototype, add roles and labels (aria-checked on substeps, aria-expanded on step heads, button semantics plus descriptive labels like 'before photo 2 of 6' on thumbnails, accessible names on icon buttons, aria-live on the toast) and give the dots and spine a non-color cue (shape or text). Treat this as a build gate on the reference implementation, not only on the native port.
findings.spec_change: Add a Verification bullet to the Accessibility section (spec.json ~line 1404) stating the requirement applies to the beta reference build, and add an explicit aria/labeling checklist row to the Part III Acceptance Criteria quality gates (~line 2465).

findings.title: Opaque AI error copy and substeps that look required but do not gate
findings.observation: When a proxy call fails for a network reason the user sees the raw message, e.g. 'AI: Failed to fetch' (SortPlanBlock line 422, CoachBlock line 500), which is meaningless to a tester and does not distinguish offline from a provider outage from a bad endpoint (only NO_ENDPOINT gets friendly copy). Separately, the substep checkboxes render as a tappable checklist with checkmarks (StepPanel line 453) that strongly imply they are required, but marking a step done ignores them entirely (line 473), so a tester can complete a step with zero substeps checked and never knows whether that was allowed.
findings.recommendation: Map AI failure reasons to plain copy ('You appear to be offline; the built-in plan still works', 'Our AI service is busy, try again', 'Check the AI endpoint in Settings'). Clarify the substep affordance: either label it 'Guidance, check as you go (optional)' or show a soft 'x of n done' nudge on the done button so the optionality is explicit.
findings.spec_change: Extend the Part III corrections row 'Substeps imply gating but do not gate' (spec.json ~line 2176) with the exact clarifying-copy decision, and add a bullet to the AI decoupling workstream (~line 2221) requiring user-facing error mapping (offline / endpoint / provider) rather than surfacing raw fetch errors.

findings.title: No team-facing beta health dashboard is defined
findings.observation: The spec defines a clean product-event taxonomy and six success metrics but never describes how the QA discipline would watch beta health. There is no defined view for crash-free rate, AI success versus failure rate broken down by reason, per-step funnel drop-off (step_completed by S, to find where sessions stall), storage-fallback incidence, or image-decode failure rate. The Beta Test Plan lists 'privacy-respecting event logging for loop milestones only' (spec.json ~line 2505) but no dashboard for the signals that tell the team whether the build itself is healthy.
findings.recommendation: Specify a small Beta Health Dashboard for the team, fed by the product events plus the new quality telemetry: a funnel tile (install to setup to zone_started to before to after to zone_completed), an AI reliability tile (success rate and failure reason breakdown for Sort Plan and Coach Review), a stability tile (crash-free sessions, app_error by screen), and a storage tile (fallback-engaged rate). All aggregate counts, no per-home data.
findings.spec_change: Add a subsection 'Beta Health Dashboard (team view)' to the Analytics & Instrumentation section or the Beta Test Plan (spec.json ~line 2508) listing these tiles and their source events, explicitly aggregate-only and with no photo, name, or free text.

reviews.summary: The MVP proves the zone-reset loop and the four signature visualizations (progress rings, six-segment spine, zone-dot strips, stat tiles) are all present, but the front-end has three structural gaps for a measured beta. First, it fires zero analytics events, so the beta cannot compute the activation and AI-attach metrics its own test plan promises. Second, the render model rebuilds the whole screen on every state change, which loses expansion state and keyboard/screen-reader focus mid-loop. Third, the core payoff, the before/after pairing, is never shown together and the AI's own before-to-after improvement is captured but never visualized, so the most motivating moment in the app is the least designed.
reviews.top_priority: Implement the privacy-safe client event layer. The code (app-review.js) fires none of the events defined in the spec's Analytics & Instrumentation taxonomy, yet the Beta Test Plan commits to measuring activation and AI attach rate. Add a single track(event, props) dispatcher with an on-device queue and the exact loop call sites, carrying counts and enums only (never a photo, household or room name, or user-typed text), before testers touch the build.

findings.title: No client instrumentation exists in the build
findings.observation: app-review.js contains no analytics dispatch at all. The Setup 'Start my reset' onclick, go('zone',...), PhotoBlock upload, the StepPanel done toggle, callAI(), and the AuditBlock buttons all mutate state and saveProg() but emit nothing. Meanwhile the spec's Analytics & Instrumentation section (line 1616) fully defines app_install, setup_complete, zone_started, before_photos_added, sort_plan_requested, step_completed, after_photos_added, coach_review_received, zone_completed, and audit_action, and the Beta Test Plan (line 2504) says 'privacy-respecting event logging for the loop milestones.' None of it is wired.
findings.recommendation: Add a single track(event, props) function backed by an on-device queue that flushes to the metered proxy. Fire the taxonomy events at the existing mutation points: setup start, go('zone') first open, photo array push (before/after), the done toggle (step enum), the callAI() begin/return for both prompts, the auto-complete branch, and the two audit buttons. Carry only counts and enums; never home.name, room name, or a photo.
findings.spec_change: Add a MUST backlog row to 'Build-Ready Feature Backlog' (line 2304): 'Client event instrumentation, a track(event,props) dispatcher wired to the loop milestones, on-device queue to the proxy' and a matching Acceptance Criteria bullet under 'Functional' (line 2452): 'The ten loop events in the Analytics taxonomy fire once each at their defined points and carry only counts and enums.'

findings.title: Whole-screen re-render loses place and focus mid-loop
findings.observation: render() does root.innerHTML='' and rebuilds the active screen. The StepPanel done toggle, the AuditBlock actions, and the product-sheet 'I own this' toggle all call render() directly. Because each StepPanel's open flag is a local closure recreated fresh, marking Sort done collapses every panel the user had expanded and rebuilds the DOM, which drops keyboard and screen-reader focus back to document top. In a six-step loop this fires up to six times per zone.
findings.recommendation: Move step-panel expansion and done state to persisted or component-local state that survives updates, and update only the affected node instead of the whole screen. At minimum, after a done toggle, restore the expanded set and move focus to the toggled step's heading. Carry this rule into the Expo port so the root re-render pattern is not reproduced.
findings.spec_change: Add a bullet to the Accessibility section (line 1382, 'Touch targets and motion' or a new 'Focus management' note): 'State changes preserve scroll position, panel expansion, and keyboard/screen-reader focus; no interaction returns focus to the top of the screen.' Add to the 'Port Plan & Module Structure' state row a note to use component-level state rather than a root innerHTML rebuild.

findings.title: Before/after payoff is never shown together
findings.observation: PhotoBlock('before') renders near the top of the Zone Runner and PhotoBlock('after') renders below all six step panels and the Coach block, so the two galleries are never on screen together. The Design System (line 580) lists 'the before and after diptych for paired evidence photos' as a signature component, but the MVP has no pairing, no diptych, and no compare view. The Coach Review references wins and remaining gaps with no adjacent visual of what changed.
findings.recommendation: Add a side-by-side before/after diptych at the point of completion (near the Coach block), reusing the compressed thumbnails already in IndexedDB. Keep the slider deferred, but the static two-up pairing is cheap and is the activation payoff the beta must earn.
findings.spec_change: Add a MUST backlog row to 'Build-Ready Feature Backlog' (line 2304): 'Before/after diptych at zone completion (side-by-side; compare slider deferred)' and add to Acceptance Criteria 'Functional' (line 2452): 'On completion the tester sees their before and after photos paired in one view.'

findings.title: Rich AI quality and outcome signals go uncaptured
findings.observation: The AI path surfaces many signals that never leave the function: NO_ENDPOINT, the 60s AbortController timeout, extractJson failure, repairParse recovery, empty-reply, and HTTP error, plus the before clutter_score (1-5) and the after score, meets_standard, wins/remaining counts. All are numbers and enums with no photo or PII. Today they are stored on prog or shown once, then lost. For a beta whose headline is AI, failure reasons, latency, and the before-to-after improvement are the most valuable privacy-safe signals available.
findings.recommendation: Emit an ai_request_failed{reason enum, latency_ms} event and extend the success events with outcome properties. Capture repair_used (whether repairParse fired), clutter_score on the Sort plan, and score, meets_standard, and a derived score-minus-clutter delta on the Coach Review. All values are integers and booleans; no image or text.
findings.spec_change: Extend the Analytics taxonomy table (line 1629): add properties to sort_plan_requested (clutter_score, latency_ms, outcome) and coach_review_received (score, meets_standard, repair_used, latency_ms), add an ai_request_failed{reason} row, and add a 'Beta AI health' metric to Success Metrics (line 1726): 'AI success rate, p50/p95 latency, and truncation-repair rate.'

findings.title: 'Items released' stat conflates relocate with released
findings.observation: zoneStats() computes items += (out.d||0)+(out.t||0)+(out.r||0), summing relocate, donate, and discard, and the Dashboard tile labels this 'items released.' Relocated items stay in the home, so counting them inflates the number. The spec's own correction row (line 2165) and Success Metrics (line 1750) both define items_released as donate plus discard only. The code and the spec disagree, and this number is the north-star stat and the share-card hook.
findings.recommendation: Compute items_released as donate plus discard, and surface relocate separately as an 'items rehomed' count if kept. Make zone_completed.items_released exclude relocate so the analytics number matches the tile.
findings.spec_change: Tighten the correction row at line 2165 to 'Fix the stat to donate plus discard; show relocate as a separate rehomed count' and add a one-line definition under Success Metrics 'Items released' (line 1750): 'relocate is excluded; it is reported separately as items rehomed.'

findings.title: 'Time invested' tile is an estimate labeled as fact
findings.observation: zoneStats() computes mins += (steps done / 6) * sum(z.t), a fraction of the static per-step time budget from the spine, and the Dashboard labels it 'time invested.' No real elapsed time is measured anywhere; prog stores only done_at and audit timestamps. The number reads as measured effort but is a projection of the authored budget, which also cannot validate the 15-to-90-minute zone claim the product rests on.
findings.recommendation: Either relabel the tile 'estimated time' honestly, or capture lightweight per-zone session seconds (start on first zone open, accumulate active time) and drive both the tile and a beta metric from real data. Session seconds is a count, privacy-safe.
findings.spec_change: Add a metric row to Success Metrics (line 1726): 'Zone session time, median active minutes per completed zone, validates the 15-to-90-minute design claim,' traced to a new zone session-time capture; and note in the Dashboard feature row (line 349) that the time tile is an estimate until session timing lands.

findings.title: Substep affordance confusion and two definitions of done
findings.observation: Substeps are checkable via the sb bitmask and visually toggle, implying they are required, but they never affect step completion, and the panels start collapsed (open.v=false) with no current-step highlight or auto-advance across the six S's. 'done' is set in two places with slightly different rules: the PhotoBlock after-upload branch (steps.every && after photos) and the StepPanel toggle (steps.every && ap.length>0). Testers cannot tell what gates progress.
findings.recommendation: Label substeps as optional guidance, show a per-step progress count (for example 'Shine, 4 of 7') matching the Accessibility section's own announcement pattern, and auto-open the next incomplete step after a done toggle. Unify the done rule in one helper called from both paths.
findings.spec_change: Expand the correction row at line 2175 ('Substeps imply gating but do not gate') into a concrete affordance spec: substeps labelled optional, a visible 'n of m' count per step, next-step auto-open, and a single canonical done predicate shared by the photo and step-toggle paths.

findings.title: No discipline dashboards defined for the beta
findings.observation: The spec defines the event taxonomy but no boards to read it. The code exposes strong front-end health signals with no home: idbReady false triggers the in-memory photo fallback (a data-loss risk), LS.set() catches quota failures with a toast, compress() runs a multi-pass quality-then-dimension loop, and render() rebuilds the whole screen. None of these are surfaced for the team.
findings.recommendation: Specify three team boards keyed to my discipline: a six-S drop-off funnel from step_completed{step} to find where sessions stall; an AI reliability panel (attach rate, failure reasons, p50/p95 latency, repair rate); and a client-health board (IndexedDB fallback rate, storage-full rate, compression pass count, cold-start white-screen rate).
findings.spec_change: Add a 'Beta dashboards' subsection under Analytics & Instrumentation (after line 1707) enumerating the three boards (six-S funnel, AI reliability, client health) and the events or signals each reads.

findings.title: Status carried by color alone and unlabeled icon controls
findings.observation: Zone-dot strips (dot done/part) and the six-segment spine (seg background swapped between STEP_C[i] and #e4dcce) convey completion by color only, with no text or shape. Icon-only buttons (the gear, the back chevron, the ＋/− tally, the panel chevrons, and '＋ Add photo') have no accessible names, photo thumbnails set background-image with no label, and toast() has no aria-live region. This contradicts the spec's own Accessibility rule (line 1374) that meaning must never rest on the six step colors alone.
findings.recommendation: Give dots and segments a non-color cue (a check glyph or fill pattern) plus an aria-label such as 'Sort done,' add aria-labels to every icon button, label thumbnails 'before photo 2 of 6,' and mark the toast container aria-live=polite. These are the same choices that help a tired user on a weekday morning.
findings.spec_change: Pull these into the Part III Acceptance Criteria 'Quality and compliance gates' (line 2464) as a beta gate: 'Dot strips and step segments carry a non-color state cue and an accessible label; all icon-only buttons and photo thumbnails have accessible names; status toasts announce via aria-live,' cross-referencing the Accessibility section.

reviews.role: Senior Back-End Engineering expert (data & telemetry architecture)
reviews.summary: The spec describes a mature event taxonomy, a household data model, and a metered AI proxy, but the runnable prototype implements none of the telemetry or metering that data collection and every dashboard depend on: app-review.js emits zero events, callAI does no logging or cost attribution, and the on-device schema overwrites the very history the retention metrics need. The core loop and on-device storage are solid, but as a data source the build is currently mute. The single biggest gap is that the pipeline from device to a privacy-respecting store, and the proxy contract that meters and logs the AI call, do not exist yet even in stub form, so no Success Metric or team dashboard can actually be computed from this beta.
reviews.top_priority: Stand up the beta telemetry foundation before testers touch it: a small on-device append-only event client with an offline queue and batched, PII-free flush, plus a proxy request/response contract that meters and logs every AI call. The Analytics & Instrumentation section names the events and the Backend Data Model names ai_usage, but nothing in the prototype produces either, so activation, AI attach rate, Sustain retention, and cost-per-analysis are all currently uncomputable from real beta data.

findings.title: No event pipeline exists; the taxonomy is defined but unemitted
findings.observation: The Analytics & Instrumentation section defines 14 events (app_install through audit_action) and the Beta Test Plan promises privacy-respecting logging of loop milestones, but app-review.js contains no analytics client, no event buffer, and no emit calls anywhere. State mutations (saveProg, go(), the done toggles, the AI buttons) fire no telemetry. A beta shipped on this code produces zero measurable signal, so Activation, AI attach rate, and Sustain retention cannot be computed.
findings.recommendation: Add a tiny on-device event client: an append-only ring buffer in its own localStorage key (for example 6smz:events), each event carrying only {name, ts, anon_install_id, zone_slug, catalog_version, enum props}, batched and flushed to an analytics endpoint on a timer and on next launch, with an offline queue so garage and basement captures are not lost. It must never carry a photo, home or room name, or user-typed text, matching the existing 'Stays on this device' promise.
findings.spec_change: Add a new subsection 'Beta event client and transport' under Analytics & Instrumentation specifying: an append-only local buffer keyed anonymously (no account in beta), a batched PII-free flush with an offline retry queue, and an explicit allowlist of event property types (counts, phase enums, zone slug, catalog version) so the section documents transport, not just the event names.

findings.title: AI proxy performs no metering or attribution; the client dictates model and token cap
findings.observation: callAI (line 202) POSTs a body with model:'claude-sonnet-4-6' and max_tokens:1200 chosen by the client, and sends no capability tag, no zone identifier, no request id, and no install id. The proxy therefore cannot populate the ai_usage entity (capability, zone_id, image_count, tokens, cost_estimate) from the Backend Data Model, cannot enforce the free-tier analysis cap the AI service hardening delta requires, and cannot stop a client from overriding the model. sort_plan_requested and coach_review_received are also not distinguishable on the wire.
findings.recommendation: Move model, max_tokens, and the cap policy server-side so the proxy owns cost, and have the client send only {capability: sort_plan|coach_review, anon_install_id, catalog_version, zone_slug, image_count}. The proxy meters per install id, writes one ai_usage row per call including latency and estimated cost, and returns a request id the client logs alongside the corresponding analytics event.
findings.spec_change: Add a 'Proxy request and response contract' table to 'The Two Decoupling Workstreams' item 2 (and cross-reference ai_usage in the Backend Data Model): columns for client-sent fields (capability enum, anon install id, catalog version, zone slug, image count) versus proxy-owned fields (model, max_tokens, per-install cap, tokens, cost_estimate, request_id), stating explicitly that the client must not select the model.

findings.title: Progress schema overwrites audit history and has no reset generation, so retention and before/after history are lost
findings.observation: zoneProg (line 242) stores a single audit timestamp and one drift boolean. Completion sets p.audit=Date.now(); every subsequent Holding or Drift tap in AuditBlock overwrites it, so only the latest audit survives. There is no separate done_at, and 'Run this zone again' (line 515) resets steps while keeping the same bp/ap arrays with no generation counter, mixing photos across runs. As a result the Sustain retention metric (an audit action in the D28 window) and any before/after compare across generations are not derivable from stored data, even though the Backend Data Model defines reset_generation on both zone_progress and photo.
findings.recommendation: Replace the scalar audit field with an append-only audits array of {ts, result: holding|drift}, add a distinct done_at, and add a reset_generation integer that increments on 'Run this zone again' and is stamped onto each photo record (side, generation, ts) so history and the compare slider have real inputs.
findings.spec_change: Update the prog row in section 5.1 Storage schema (and the beta on-device equivalent) to read: step booleans, substep bitmasks, done_at, an append-only audit log [{ts, result}], drift flag, reset_generation, and photo records carrying {side, generation, ts}; and note in the audit_action event definition that each audit appends rather than overwrites.

findings.title: The AI reliability layer and storage fallbacks emit no health telemetry
findings.observation: The spec claims the reliability layer was validated in harness, but in the field nothing is measured. AI failures are only shown to the user via toast (callAI catch blocks, 'AI: '+err.message), the 60s AbortController timeout is silent, and repairParse recovering a truncated reply leaves no trace. On storage, openIDB failure drops to an in-memory photo map with a one-time boot toast (line 581), and LS.set surfaces 'Storage full' as a toast (line 125). Losing photos is an activation killer, yet none of these degraded states are counted, so the team cannot see the real timeout rate, parse-repair rate, or how often testers silently run session-only photos.
findings.recommendation: Emit health events with enum reasons and coarse buckets, no payloads: ai_call_failed{reason: no_endpoint|timeout|http_error|empty|parse_failed}, ai_response_repaired (parser backtracked), ai_latency_bucket, ai_image_bytes_bucket, and storage_degraded{mode: memory_only|write_failed}. These feed a reliability panel and validate the harness claims against real devices.
findings.spec_change: Add a 'Health and quality signals' event table to Analytics & Instrumentation (distinct from the behavioral taxonomy) listing ai_call_failed with a reason enum, ai_response_repaired, ai_latency_bucket, and storage_degraded, and add a beta target row such as 'AI success rate' and 'photo persistence rate' to Success Metrics.

findings.title: items_released is computed three different ways; the correction row is now stale
findings.observation: zoneStats (line 243) computes the dashboard 'items released' stat as donate + discard + relocate (p.out.d + p.out.t + p.out.r). But Success Metrics defines Items released as donate plus discard, and the zone_completed event property is specified as the donate plus discard tally. Meanwhile the Part III correction row still says the dashboard 'omits relocate' and totals donate plus discard only, which is the opposite of what this build now does. Three sources, three definitions, for the north-star stat and the share-card hook.
findings.recommendation: Pin one canonical definition. Recommend items_released = donate + discard (relocations stay in the home, so they are not releases) and keep relocated as a separate displayed count if useful. Compute the emitted event property from the same function that renders the user stat so they never diverge.
findings.spec_change: Reconcile three places to one definition: fix the stale correction row in 'What the Code Analysis Confirmed and Corrected' (it describes the pre-fix behavior, not this build), and confirm the zone_completed.items_released event property and the Items released metric both read donate plus discard, with relocate tracked separately.

findings.title: Time invested is a synthetic estimate, not measured elapsed time
findings.observation: The Dashboard 'time invested' stat is computed in zoneStats as (steps completed / 6) times the sum of the zone's per-step minute estimates (z.t). No real session timing is captured anywhere: there is no zone_opened_at, no step timestamps, no dwell tracking. So the number shown to the user, and the 'time spent' value the future before/after share card depends on, is a plan estimate dressed as a measurement. It also cannot answer where sessions stall in real time.
findings.recommendation: Capture lightweight session timing on device: a zone_opened timestamp, per-step first-touch and done timestamps, and accumulate real active dwell (guarded against backgrounding). Show measured time where available and fall back to the estimate only until real data exists. This also gives the funnel a real 'time to first finished zone'.
findings.spec_change: Add a note to the Dashboard capability row (Feature Inventory) and to Success Metrics that time invested is an estimate until session timing lands, and add events zone_opened and step_dwell (elapsed bucket) to the taxonomy so the share-card time value and stall analysis use measured time.

findings.title: No beta aggregation or team dashboard is specified for the events
findings.observation: The event taxonomy and Success Metrics exist, but there is no defined server-side aggregation or serving layer that turns raw events into the funnel and health views a back-end or growth reviewer would watch during the 14-day closed test. The Beta Test Plan says 'what to measure' but not how the numbers are rolled up, retained, or displayed, so the pipeline currently has a mouth (events) and no stomach.
findings.recommendation: Define a thin aggregation layer: server rollups for the activation funnel (install to setup to zone_started to before/after to zone_completed), AI attach and success rates, and a reliability panel from the health events, with a short bounded retention window for raw beta events and cohort-by-install-day grouping. This is small because the beta has no accounts, only anonymous install ids.
findings.spec_change: Add a 'Beta backend aggregation and dashboard' subsection to Part III (near Beta Test Plan) specifying the rollup tables, the funnel and reliability panels, the anonymous-install-id cohort key, and a raw-event retention window, so the discipline dashboard is a build artifact rather than an implied one.

findings.title: Catalog version is not stamped on-device or on any event
findings.observation: The DATA object is embedded inline with no version stamp, and neither the prog records nor the cached AI plans (p.ai, p.aiA) record which catalog produced them. The Backend Data Model defines a catalog_version entity and the Live catalog delta relies on version stamps, but in the beta build there is no way to tie a field observation, an AI plan, or a product reference to a catalog release, and a refreshed catalog cannot invalidate stale cached plans.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a CATALOG_VERSION constant now, persist it into home and into each prog record when a plan is cached, include it as a property on every analytics and ai_usage payload, and mark cached AI plans stale when the version changes.
findings.spec_change: Add a catalog_version field to the beta on-device state in section 5.1 and to the event property allowlist, and note in 'The Two Decoupling Workstreams' that even the embedded beta catalog carries a version stamp so field data and the later live catalog service share one key.

findings.title: No in-app feedback capture for the one question the beta must answer
findings.observation: The stated whole-test question is whether a tester wants to do the next zone, and the Beta Test Plan wants qualitative feedback on exactly that, but the app has no feedback affordance and no way to capture it as data. There is also no distinction between a first AI request and a rebuild: the SortPlanBlock and CoachBlock buttons relabel to 'Rebuild plan' and 'Review again' but emit nothing, so repeated AI use (a strong or a frustrated signal) is invisible.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight post-completion micro-prompt (a one-tap 'want to do another zone?' yes or not now, and a thumbs on whether the AI plan and review were useful), stored as events only with no free text leaving the device unless the user opts to send it. Distinguish sort_plan_requested first-call from a rebuild count.
findings.spec_change: Add events next_zone_intent{answer}, ai_plan_useful{capability, verdict}, and ai_plan_rebuilt (increment) to the taxonomy, and add a corresponding qualitative row to the Beta Test Plan 'What to measure' so the next-zone signal is captured as data rather than only anecdote.

reviews.summary: The spec has a strong, well articulated growth thesis (the 1:1 content-to-zone funnel in U7 and a clean event taxonomy in U11), but the MVP build does not yet exercise any of it: app-review.js emits zero analytics events, has no share surface, and captures nothing about where a tester came from. The single most valuable growth asset the model names, the before/after share card, is deferred entirely from the beta even though the app already holds every field the card needs on-device. The result is a beta that can prove the reset loop works but cannot measure or ignite the viral and attribution loops the launch depends on.
reviews.top_priority: Bring a minimal on-device before/after share card into the beta (no backend, photos leave only on an explicit user share) and pair it with a first-party deep-link attribution event, so the beta can actually test the "markets at the zone" viral loop and per-content acquisition instead of shipping blind on both.

findings.title: The viral surface (before/after share card) is cut from the beta despite being buildable on-device today
findings.observation: The entire GTM thesis in the 'Go-to-Market & the Content Funnel' section makes the branded before/after share card the 'Advocate' stage and the only zero-cost organic acquisition surface, and the app already holds every field that card needs: before/after photo ids in p.bp and p.ap, the zone name z.n, time via fmtMin, and an items count in zoneStats(). Yet the MVP cut-line table (line 2049) and the 'Explicitly Deferred' list (line 2535) push share cards entirely past the beta, and app-review.js has no export or share path anywhere. The beta can prove the reset loop but cannot test the viral loop the whole growth model rests on.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal on-device share-card generator to the beta: render the before/after diptych plus zone name, minutes invested, and items released to a canvas and hand it to the native share sheet or camera roll. No server and no account required, so it fits the on-device privacy posture, and photos leave the device only on an explicit user share action.
findings.spec_change: In 'MVP Beta: Definition & Scope' move the before/after share card from the Deferred column of the cut-line table into the In-the-beta column, scoped as an on-device, no-backend card; add a matching MUST/NICE row to the Build-Ready Feature Backlog; and add a 'share_card_generated' row to the U11 event taxonomy.

findings.title: The beta build emits no analytics events at all, so it would ship blind on activation and AI attach rate
findings.observation: The task describes app-review.js as carrying 'events,' but the code emits none: there is no track() helper and no event call at any milestone, not at setup_complete (Setup start button, line 274), not at zone auto-complete (line 387 and line 474), not at the Sort plan call (line 421), the coach review (line 499), or the audit taps (lines 513-514). The U11 taxonomy exists on paper only, and the Beta Test Plan's 'Instrumentation' row (line 2504) promises loop-milestone logging that nothing implements. The two things the beta must measure, activation and AI attach rate, cannot be computed.
findings.recommendation: Implement a tiny first-party event sink in the beta that writes the U11 loop events (setup_complete, zone_started, before_photos_added, sort_plan_requested, step_completed, after_photos_added, coach_review_received, zone_completed with items_released, audit_action) to local storage with an opt-in manual export. No third-party SDK, no advertising identifier, no cross-app tracking, consistent with the U11 privacy stance.
findings.spec_change: Add a MUST row to the Build-Ready Feature Backlog: 'Privacy-respecting local event logging for the U11 loop milestones (no third-party SDK, exportable)'; and add a bullet under 'Acceptance Criteria > Quality and compliance gates' that the loop milestone events fire and are inspectable and exportable on a physical device.

findings.title: No attribution event exists, so the '1:1 content-to-zone deep link' thesis cannot be measured
findings.observation: The GTM core mechanic ('markets at the zone,' the 1:1 deep link from Shorts and episodes to the exact zone) has no instrumentation. In U11, app_install is the sole top-of-funnel denominator and carries no source property, there is no deep_link_opened event, and Setup() (line 259) records nothing about origin. Marketing cannot attribute a qualified install to a specific Short, episode, the book, or the manual, cannot compute a per-zone funnel, and cannot prove the deep-link thesis or rank content by installs it drives.
findings.recommendation: Add a first-party, privacy-respecting attribution event: deep_link_opened with a coarse channel enum (short, episode, book, manual, direct), a content_id, and the target zone slug, resolved from campaign parameters carried in the deep link itself. No ad identifier, no device graph, no App Tracking Transparency prompt, in keeping with the U11 privacy stance.
findings.spec_change: Add a 'deep_link_opened' row (properties: channel enum, content_id, target_zone_slug) and a 'source' property on app_install to the Analytics event taxonomy table; add a 'Per-content / per-zone acquisition' metric row to Success Metrics traced to those events.

findings.title: The completion moment, the peak worth sharing, passes with a bare re-render
findings.observation: When a zone auto-completes (p.done is set at line 387 when the after photo lands with all six steps done, and again at line 474), ZoneScreen simply re-renders and appends the AuditBlock. The Coach Review returns a score, wins, and a meets_standard verdict, but there is no celebration, no surfacing of the before/after transformation, and no prompt to share. The single highest-emotion moment in the loop, the 'change they could not un-see,' is neither reinforced for retention nor turned into advocacy.
findings.recommendation: On zone_completed, show a completion moment that pairs the before/after, shows time invested and items released, echoes the coach score, and offers a one-tap 'Share this win' that feeds the share card in finding 1. This is simultaneously the motivation peak (usability) and the growth trigger (advocacy).
findings.spec_change: Add a 'zone-completion celebration with before/after recap and share CTA' item to the Zone Runner row of 'Feature Inventory by Screen' and to the MVP Build-Ready Feature Backlog, and reference it from the 'Advocate' row of the U7 funnel table as the in-app trigger for share-card creation.

findings.title: No defined marketing funnel or channel visualization for the team
findings.observation: The Analytics section defines events and Success Metrics defines six metrics, but nothing specifies how marketing sees the data. The U7 funnel is described as six named stages (Discover, Trust, Install, Activate, Convert, Advocate) yet no artifact maps the events onto a viewable funnel or a per-content acquisition breakdown, so the discipline has metrics without a dashboard.
findings.recommendation: Specify a marketing dashboard: a stage funnel (app_install to setup_complete to zone_started to activation via zone_completed to share_card_generated) with step-to-step conversion; a per-content and per-zone acquisition table (deep_link_opened to install to activation); and a virality panel (cards generated per activated user, and installs attributed to shares).
findings.spec_change: Add a 'Marketing dashboards' subsection to 'Analytics & Instrumentation' defining the activation funnel chart, the per-content acquisition table, and the share/virality panel, each traced to the named events that feed it.

findings.title: Items-released hero stat is computed differently from the metric and share-card hook it feeds
findings.observation: zoneStats() (line 243) computes the dashboard 'items released' number as donate + discard + relocate (out.d + out.t + out.r), but the spec defines items_released as donate plus discard only (the zone_completed property at line 1678 and the Items-released metric at line 1750). The backlog itself flags 'fix the relocate omission if kept' (line 2368). Because that same number is the motivational north-star stat, the intended share-card hook, and a success metric, the hero and shareable figure will not match the metric it is supposed to feed.
findings.recommendation: Choose one formula and use it everywhere. Recommend keeping relocate as its own visible tally but excluding it from items_released, since relocated items are not released from the home, aligning the dashboard stat, the zone_completed property, and the future share-card hook to a single number.
findings.spec_change: Add a note to the items_released event property and the Items-released metric row fixing the formula to donate + discard, and add an Acceptance Criteria bullet that the dashboard stat, the event property, and the share card all use the identical formula.

findings.title: The app never points back to the content funnel that recruits its users
findings.observation: The beta recruits from the content ecosystem (book, manual, and the 114-video series per the Beta Test Plan at line 2482) and the funnel is framed as one shared skeleton, but the app has no surface pointing back to that content. The ZoneScreen mission card (line 349) shows function, done-state, hazard, and expert cue with no link to the matching zone video or book chapter, so the content-to-app relationship is one-directional in the build and the video series gets no in-app placement.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional per-zone 'Watch the 2-minute reset' link on the mission card that deep-links out to the matching episode or Short where one exists, starting with the Entryway which is already fully produced (spec line 944), and instrument a content_link_tapped event. Purely additive and low maintenance.
findings.spec_change: Add a 'content link' field to the Zone Runner mission-card row in 'Feature Inventory by Screen' and a 'content_link_tapped' event to the Analytics taxonomy.

findings.title: Setup captures no referral source, missing word-of-mouth and offline channel signal
findings.observation: Setup() (line 259) collects only an optional household name and the room selection. Because the beta has no accounts and deep-link attribution cannot see word-of-mouth or an offline mention of the book or a video, marketing has no way to learn how community testers actually arrived.
findings.recommendation: Add one optional, single-tap 'How did you hear about us?' enum at setup (book, video or Shorts, friend, other; skippable), stored locally and included in the exportable beta event log. No free text and no PII, so it stays privacy-safe.
findings.spec_change: Add an optional referral-source enum to the Setup capability row in 'Feature Inventory by Screen' and a 'referral_source_selected' event (enum property only) to the Analytics taxonomy, scoped to the beta.

reviews.role: Senior Customer Success expert (onboarding, activation, habit formation, retention)
reviews.summary: The core loop is strong and the value promise ("see the change from the doorway") is genuinely activating, but the build fights its own activation gate: first-run drops the tester into a 37-zone program instead of steering them to one fast win, and the payoff moment (the paired before/after) is never actually shown in-app. The Sustain loop, which is the product's own retention engine, is present but data-thin: it overwrites its own history, hardcodes a 7-day cadence that ignores what the methodology teaches, and never captures the owner or trigger that make a habit stick. The event taxonomy is clean and privacy-respecting but under-instrumented for Customer Success: it cannot see real time-to-finish, AI quality, stalls, or a tester's intent to continue, and the spec defines success metrics with no dashboards or health segmentation to act on them.
reviews.top_priority: Rebuild first-run as an activation-first flow that funnels the tester to a single fast-win zone and then shows the paired before/after so the value lands in the first sitting. Everything downstream (retention, referral, subscription) is gated on that first finished zone, and today the app scatters attention across 37 preselected zones and never renders the one image comparison that proves the change.

findings.title: First-run dumps a 37-zone program instead of guiding to one fast win
findings.observation: Setup() preselects all 6 rooms (chosen = new Set(ROOMS.map...)) so the tester lands on a dashboard of 37 zones and roughly 98 hours of work. The Dashboard 'Next up' logic just walks activeRooms in room order and picks the first not-done zone (Entryway first), not the shortest or easiest. There is no walkthrough of what 6S means, no explanation of the loop, and the value promise appears once in the setup hero then never again. This directly contradicts the spec's own guidance in Success Metrics ('onboarding sells the single 15-minute zone rather than the full multi-room program') and the beta's stated one thing to earn ('A tester finishes a real zone in one sitting... and wants to do the next one').
findings.recommendation: Make onboarding activation-first: after setup, recommend ONE starter zone chosen by shortest total time (z.t.reduce sum), open it directly with a one-screen explainer of the six steps and the before/after payoff, and treat browsing the full program as a secondary action. Rank 'Next up' by estimated time for the first two completions, then by room order.
findings.spec_change: Add a new Part III subsection 'Activation-First Onboarding' after 'MVP Beta: Definition & Scope' specifying: a suggested fast-win starter zone (ranked by shortest z.t), a first-run loop explainer, and a rule that the dashboard's first two 'Next up' picks optimize for time-to-first-finish. Add an event row first_zone_suggested (properties: room, estimated_minutes) to the Analytics & Instrumentation taxonomy, sitting between setup_complete and zone_started.

findings.title: The before/after payoff is stored but never shown paired in-app
findings.observation: PhotoBlock renders before photos (p.bp) and after photos (p.ap) in two separate galleries in separate cards, and the after-prompt to the AI even sends before-then-after images, but the app never renders a before-next-to-after comparison for the user. The entire product promise is 'a change they could not un-see' and 'see the change from the doorway,' yet the one visualization that delivers that emotional proof does not exist. The spec only defers before/after SHARE cards; it never specs an in-app comparison view, so this gap is invisible in the current plan.
findings.recommendation: Add an in-app paired before/after view (side-by-side or a swipe/slider) that appears at zone completion and on the completed zone screen, pulling the first before and first after photo from IndexedDB. This is distinct from a shareable card and stays fully on-device.
findings.spec_change: Add a MUST row to the Build-Ready Feature Backlog table: 'In-app before/after paired view (on-device, not a share card) | MUST | The core payoff; both photos already captured, only the render is missing.' Note in the Explicitly Deferred list that only the SHARE card is deferred, not the in-app comparison.

findings.title: No in-app capture of satisfaction, AI quality, or intent to continue
findings.observation: The beta's whole test is qualitative ('whether testers want the next zone', per the Beta Test Plan), yet there is no in-app instrument for it. SortPlanBlock and CoachBlock render AI output with no thumbs-up/down or 'was this right for my zone' control, so AI quality is never scored by the user. There is no post-completion prompt asking if the tester wants the next zone, and no lightweight CSAT/NPS. Failed AI calls surface only as a transient toast() and are never recorded. Customer Success is left blind on the two things it most needs: did the guidance land, and do they want more.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-tap AI-quality control (helpful / not helpful) on both the Sort plan and coach review, a single post-completion prompt ('Start your next zone?' yes/not now) that both nudges and measures intent, and an occasional lightweight satisfaction question. All answers are enums stored on-device and sent as counts only, no free text off device.
findings.spec_change: Add three event rows to the Analytics taxonomy: ai_feedback (properties: surface = sort_plan|coach_review, verdict = helpful|not_helpful), next_zone_intent (properties: response = start_next|not_now, fired after zone_completed), and beta_satisfaction (property: score enum). Add a 'Perceived value' metric to Success Metrics traced to next_zone_intent and ai_feedback.

findings.title: The richest household-health signals (clutter score, coach score, before/after delta) are computed but never instrumented
findings.observation: The AI already returns a before clutter_score (1 to 5) stored on p.ai and an after score plus meets_standard stored on p.aiA. These quantify whether a home actually improved, which is the truest thriving-vs-at-risk signal a home app can have. But the event taxonomy carries none of it: coach_review_received and zone_completed record no score, no meets_standard, and no before-to-after delta. AI failures and empty replies (callAI throws, caught into a toast) are also uninstrumented, so a tester repeatedly hitting AI errors looks identical to a happy one.
findings.recommendation: Attach the already-available quality values to existing events (privacy-safe: they are small integers and booleans, no photo or text), and add failure events so friction is visible. Compute a per-zone improvement delta from clutter_before minus a mapped after score.
findings.spec_change: In the Analytics taxonomy, add properties clutter_before to sort_plan_requested, score_after and meets_standard to coach_review_received, and improvement_delta to zone_completed. Add two rows: sort_plan_failed and coach_review_failed (property: reason = no_endpoint|timeout|empty|parse_error). Add a 'Home improvement' health metric to Success Metrics traced to improvement_delta and meets_standard.

findings.title: The Sustain retention engine loses its own history and ignores the cadence it teaches
findings.observation: AuditBlock records only a single p.drift boolean and a single p.audit timestamp, both overwritten on every audit, so the audit log is one bit deep. The dashboard 'due' rule is hardcoded to 7 days (now - p.audit > 7*864e5) regardless of the weekly-vs-monthly cadence the Sustain substeps explicitly teach, and the methodology's own rule ('two failed audits in a row means the standard is wrong, redesign') cannot fire because consecutive drift is never counted. The Sustain step also tells users to name an owner and anchor a trigger (substeps at i===5), and settings even carries an unused owner field, but neither the owner nor the trigger nor a chosen cadence is ever captured. The retention loop is present in UI but structurally cannot learn.
findings.recommendation: Store an append-only audit log per zone (timestamp + result) instead of one boolean, capture the owner, reset trigger, and chosen cadence during the Sustain step, drive the 'due' banner off the chosen cadence, and fire a redesign nudge after two consecutive drift results.
findings.spec_change: Add properties consecutive_drift and cadence to the audit_action event, and add an audit_cadence_set event (property: cadence = weekly|monthly) plus zone_owner_set fired from the Sustain step. Add a bullet to 'The Two Decoupling Workstreams' persistence section: 'Store an append-only per-zone audit log (timestamp, result) rather than a single drift flag, so Sustain retention and the two-consecutive-drift redesign rule are computable.'

findings.title: Success Metrics exist but there are no Customer Success dashboards or health segmentation
findings.observation: The spec defines a clean six-metric table but no visualizations for the team to act on it. The step_completed event carries a step property (one of the six S) that makes a step-level activation funnel trivial to build, yet no funnel view is specified. Sustain retention is defined as a single D28 number with no cohort curve. Nothing defines a household-health composite that would let Customer Success separate thriving households (activated, momentum, audits holding) from at-risk ones (stalled, drifting, AI errors), so lifecycle intervention has nothing to target.
findings.recommendation: Specify three team-facing views: an activation funnel broken down by the six S (install to setup to zone_started to before to each step to after to completed), a cohort retention grid by install week for audit_action, and a household-health score banding accounts into thriving / steady / at-risk from activation, recency, audit-holding ratio, and AI-error rate.
findings.spec_change: Add a subsection 'Customer Success Dashboards & Health Segmentation' to the Analytics & Instrumentation section defining: (1) a six-S activation funnel from step_completed.step, (2) a D0/D7/D28 cohort retention grid on audit_action by install cohort, and (3) a household_health score with thriving/steady/at-risk bands and the inputs feeding each band.

findings.title: The 'time invested' stat is fabricated from static estimates, not real elapsed time
findings.observation: zoneStats() computes 'time invested' as (steps done / 6) times the sum of the static per-step estimates z.t, so the dashboard's motivational time number is an estimate of planned time scaled by progress, never a measurement of what the tester actually spent. Nothing captures real session duration. That makes the stat both mildly misleading to users and useless to Customer Success for diagnosing activation friction (how long does a first zone really take, and where do long sittings correlate with abandonment).
findings.recommendation: Capture real elapsed time per zone (from zone_started to zone_completed, pausing across app backgrounding) and drive the dashboard stat from it, or relabel the current stat as 'estimated time' until real timing lands. Real duration is a numeric count, fully privacy-safe.
findings.spec_change: Add property session_minutes (actual, clamped) to the zone_completed event and a 'Time to first finish' metric to Success Metrics traced to zone_started and zone_completed. Add a correction row to 'What the Code Analysis Confirmed and Corrected': 'Time-invested stat is estimate-based | zoneStats scales static z.t by fraction of steps done | Back it with measured elapsed time or relabel as estimated.'

findings.title: No lifecycle model or at-risk nudge for stalled zones
findings.observation: The dashboard has a 'Pick up where you left off' card and a completed-zone 'due for a check-in' banner, but nothing detects or responds to a stalled zone: one that is started (p.steps.some(Boolean)) and not done and untouched for days. A tester who opens a zone, does two steps, and drifts away is the classic at-risk pattern, and the app neither flags it internally nor nudges the user back. With push notifications rightly deferred, the in-app lifecycle nudge is the only re-engagement lever in the beta and it is unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Define lifecycle stages (new, activated, momentum, stalled, dormant, drifting) and a matching in-app nudge for each (for stalled: surface the exact half-finished zone with 'You are three steps from done'; for drifting: prompt the two-minute audit). Fire a stall signal when a started, not-done zone sees no progress within a set window.
findings.spec_change: Add an event row zone_stalled (fires when a started, not-done zone has no step activity for 72 hours; property: steps_done). Add a 'Lifecycle stages and in-app nudges' table to the new Customer Success subsection mapping each stage to its trigger event and its in-app nudge, explicitly in-app only for the beta with push deferred.

reviews.role: Support (failure surfaces, self-serve help, diagnostics, and support-data privacy)
reviews.summary: From a Support lens this MVP is quietly ticket-generating: nearly every failure path (storage full, in-memory photo fallback, AI endpoint down, timeout, decode failure, malformed AI JSON) surfaces as a 3.4-second global toast or fails silently, and the app has no in-app help, no feedback or bug-report path, and no way to export a diagnostic bundle. Because the sensitive asset is photos of people's homes, testers cannot safely screenshot problems, so a photo-free state export is the single highest-leverage support affordance the beta is missing. The spec's Analytics section is funnel-only and has no health or reliability signals, and Success Metrics has no team-facing support or reliability dashboard, so tickets would arrive with no telemetry to triage them against.
reviews.top_priority: Add a user-triggerable, photo-free diagnostic export plus an in-app "Report a problem" path, and back it with a health and reliability event family. Home photos being sensitive means support cannot rely on screenshots, so a redacted state export (app version, storage mode, per-zone photo/step counts, last N error codes with enum error classes, endpoint reachability with the URL hostname only) is what lets a ticket be resolved without ever seeing the inside of someone's home.

findings.title: No in-app help, feedback, or diagnostic export; home photos block screenshot-based support
findings.observation: app-review.js has no help, FAQ, contact, or feedback affordance anywhere; Settings offers only 'Erase everything' and a static 'v0.1' footer. There is no way for a TestFlight or Play closed-tester to report a problem from inside the app or to attach any state. Because the whole product is built around photos of the tester's home, they cannot safely screenshot a broken screen to a support inbox, so tickets will arrive as vague prose ('AI didn't work') with nothing attached.
findings.recommendation: Add a Settings 'Report a problem / Send feedback' entry that (a) opens a short structured feedback capture and (b) generates a copyable, photo-free diagnostic bundle: app/build version, storage mode (IndexedDB vs in-memory), whether an AI endpoint is set and its reachability, per-zone counts of steps done and photos held (no images, no home or room names), and the last N error codes as enum classes. Explicitly exclude photo data, the household name, room names, and the raw endpoint URL.
findings.spec_change: Add a Part III backlog row 'In-app help + feedback + photo-free diagnostic export | MUST' to the Build-Ready Feature Backlog table, and add a bullet to Acceptance Criteria > Functional: 'A tester can trigger a diagnostic export that contains no photo, home name, room name, or endpoint URL, and can report a problem in-app.'

findings.title: Persistence failures are silent or one-time; in-memory photo mode loses photos with a misleading on-screen promise
findings.observation: LS.set catches quota errors, fires a transient toast ('Storage full; some data may not persist.') and returns false, but every caller (saveProg, saveGear, settings writes) ignores the return value, so step completions, tallies, and cached AI plans can silently fail to persist. When IndexedDB is unavailable, putPhoto falls back to an in-memory object (memPhotos) that is lost on reload, announced only by a single boot toast the user will often miss, while every PhotoBlock still prints the fixed reassurance 'Stays on this device.' There is no signal collected when either failure occurs, so support cannot tell a 'my progress disappeared' ticket from user error.
findings.recommendation: Persist a storage-mode flag and count write failures. Emit a health signal on each persistence failure and on entering in-memory photo mode. On screen, replace the always-on 'Stays on this device' label with the true state when running in memory ('Photos in this session are not saved; reopen over http to keep them').
findings.spec_change: Add two events to Analytics & Instrumentation > Event taxonomy: 'storage_mode' (fires once at boot; property mode = persistent | session_only) and 'storage_write_failed' (property surface = progress | gear | photo). Add a row to Known Limitations or Beta Compliance noting that the in-memory fallback must show an honest persistent notice rather than the 'stays on device' copy.

findings.title: AI failures surface as raw transient toasts with no retry, no cancel, and a silent 60-second wait
findings.observation: callAI runs a single fetch bounded by a 60s AbortController and no retry, so a hung or failing proxy leaves the button reading 'Reading your photos…' for a full minute with no progress or cancel, then dumps a raw error into a 3.4s toast ('AI: Failed to fetch', 'AI: The user aborted a request'). This contradicts the spec's Part I reliability-layer claim of 'one automatic retry with backoff on failure'; that retry is not present in this ported build. Timeouts, CORS errors, HTTP 5xx, empty replies, and unrepairable JSON all collapse into the same cryptic verbatim toast, which is a direct driver of 'the AI is broken' tickets and one-star beta reviews.
findings.recommendation: Classify AI errors into a small enum, show a persistent (not 3.4s) failure state on the Sort Plan / Coach blocks with a Retry button, add a Cancel affordance and a visible expectation during the wait, and reconcile the missing retry-with-backoff against the Part I claim so the spec and code agree.
findings.spec_change: Correct the Part I AI Subsystem > Reliability layer bullet to state that automatic retry is a build-time requirement not yet in the ported beta code, and add an 'ai_call_failed' event to the Event taxonomy with property error_class = no_endpoint | timeout | network | http_error | empty_reply | parse_failure, plus an 'ai_latency_ms' property on coach_review_received and sort_plan_requested.

findings.title: No error boundary and no AI-JSON validation; a bad render or garbled reply white-screens or shows nonsense with no capture
findings.observation: The app has no top-level error boundary (the spec itself flags this in Port Plan), so any render throw white-screens with nothing logged. AI output is rendered without clamping: SortPlanBlock prints `Clutter ${a.clutter_score||'?'}/5` and CoachBlock prints `${a.score}/5`, so a model reply with score 7 or a missing field renders '7/5' or 'undefined/5'. The spec P1 gate calls for runtime JSON validation but this build has none. Both failure modes produce support contacts with zero diagnostic trail.
findings.recommendation: Add a top-level error boundary that renders a recovery screen offering the diagnostic export and a 'return to dashboard' action, and clamp/validate AI JSON (score and clutter to 1-5, default arrays) before render. Emit an app_error signal on boundary catch.
findings.spec_change: Promote the two items in Part III (error boundary in Port Plan; JSON clamping in Beta Compliance P1) into Acceptance Criteria > Quality and compliance gates as explicit pass conditions, and add an 'app_error' event (property error_class, screen) to the Analytics event taxonomy.

findings.title: Analytics taxonomy is funnel-only; there are no health or reliability signals to triage tickets against
findings.observation: The Analytics & Instrumentation section defines 14 behavioral funnel events (install through audit_action) but not one health or failure signal. Support therefore has no way to know whether a spike in 'AI broken' tickets corresponds to a real proxy outage, whether photo decode is failing on certain devices, or how often the truncation-repair path (repairParse) is even invoked. The privacy discipline is already well-established in that section (counts, phases, enums only; no photo, name, or free text), so a health family can inherit the same rules cleanly.
findings.recommendation: Add a named 'Health & Reliability signals' event family that reuses the section's existing privacy contract: ai_call_failed (error_class), ai_latency_ms, storage_write_failed, storage_mode, photo_decode_failed, json_repair_invoked, and app_error. No payload carries a photo, home or room name, free text, or the raw endpoint URL.
findings.spec_change: Add a new subsection 'Health & Reliability signals' under Analytics & Instrumentation, immediately after the Event taxonomy table, listing those seven events with when-they-fire and why-it-matters columns, and extend the existing 'Privacy stance' callout to state that health events carry only enum error classes, latencies, and counts.

findings.title: No team-facing Support & Reliability dashboard; Success Metrics is conversion-only
findings.observation: Success Metrics defines six funnel and revenue metrics (activation, AI attach, sustain retention, items released, kit conversion, subscription conversion) but nothing my discipline can watch. During a 12-plus tester, 14-day closed beta there is no visualization of AI failure rate by error class, in-memory fallback incidence, photo-decode failure rate, crash/error-boundary rate, or ticket volume mapped to the loop stage where users stall. Without it, support volume cannot be correlated to a build or a proxy incident.
findings.recommendation: Define a Support & Reliability dashboard fed by the health event family: AI failure rate broken down by error_class over sort_plan_requested + coach_review_received, storage session-only incidence, photo_decode_failed rate, app_error (crash) rate, and self-reported ticket count bucketed by loop stage, each sliced by app/build version. Keep it aggregate-only with no per-household drill-down so support data stays private.
findings.spec_change: Add a 'Support & Reliability dashboard' subsection to Success Metrics (or a companion section) with a metrics table: AI failure rate by class, storage session-only rate, decode-failure rate, crash-free rate, and ticket volume by loop stage, each 'traced to' the new health events and each stated as aggregate-only with no home-level identifiers.

findings.title: AI endpoint field has no validation or test-connection, and its URL can leak a token into any export
findings.observation: The Settings AI endpoint is a free-text field saved verbatim to localStorage on every keystroke, with no validation and no way to test it; a typo or a wrong path only fails later as a cryptic fetch error at call time, driving 'AI not working' tickets. Worse, a proxy URL can legitimately carry a token or key in its path or query string, so any naive diagnostic export or log that includes the endpoint would leak a credential and defeat the app's 'no key in the app' posture.
findings.recommendation: Add basic URL validation and a 'Test connection' button that makes a lightweight probe and reports a clear pass/fail, reducing endpoint-misconfiguration tickets. Establish a redaction rule: diagnostics and any health event record at most the endpoint hostname, never the full URL, path, or query string.
findings.spec_change: Add a bullet to Beta Compliance & Privacy Gates (P1): 'The AI endpoint URL is never included in diagnostics, exports, or telemetry beyond its hostname, since it may carry a proxy token,' and add an 'Endpoint validation + test-connection' row to the Part III Build-Ready Feature Backlog (NICE).

findings.title: The headline AI button dead-ends for the majority of testers, who have no proxy
findings.observation: AI is off by default (no endpoint), which the README confirms is the expected beta state for most testers. Yet the Sort Plan block always renders an actionable 'Build my Sort plan' button and the body invites the user to tap it; with no endpoint, tapping only fires a transient toast pointing to Settings. Most testers, who cannot stand up a key-holding proxy, will experience the product's flagship differentiator as a button that does nothing, and will report it as broken.
findings.recommendation: When no endpoint is configured, replace the actionable button and 'tap below' copy with an explicit empty state ('AI coaching is off in this beta build; work the six steps with the built-in guidance'), so the static-guidance path reads as the intended experience rather than a failure.
findings.spec_change: Add a note to the Part III 'AI Sort Plan and Coach Review via proxy (MUST, conditional)' backlog row: 'When no endpoint is configured, the AI blocks must render an explicit off-state, not an actionable dead-end button,' and reflect it in Acceptance Criteria > Functional under graceful degradation to the static plan.

reviews.role: Senior Product Manager (prioritization and the value loop)
reviews.summary: The beta has a genuinely solid core loop and the spec's funnel thinking is mature, but the build cannot yet prove its own central hypotheses. app-review.js emits zero analytics events despite a well-designed 14-event taxonomy in the spec, the AI differentiator is gated behind a manual endpoint testers will never configure, and the activation payoff (the before/after reveal that should make a tester want the next zone) is collected but never plated. The retention engine and the north-star metric are both wired to thin or inconsistent signals. Fix instrumentation, the activation reveal, and AI reachability and the beta becomes a learning machine instead of a demo.
reviews.top_priority: Ship on-device instrumentation for the loop milestones in the beta build. The beta's stated job is to answer "does a household reach a finished zone with before and after photos, and then keep going," yet app-review.js contains no event capture at all, so that question is unanswerable from data. Nothing else in the funnel matters if the funnel is invisible.

findings.title: Beta ships with no instrumentation; the funnel is invisible
findings.observation: The spec's Analytics & Instrumentation section defines a clean 14-event taxonomy (app_install through audit_action), but app-review.js implements none of it. There is no track/logEvent call, no event queue, no local counter. The build only writes prog, gear, home, and settings to localStorage. The Beta Test Plan promises 'privacy-respecting event logging for the loop milestones,' and every Success Metric traces to events that do not exist in the build.
findings.recommendation: Implement an on-device event log in the beta itself, not deferred to the backend. Store loop-milestone events locally (append-only, counts and enums only, no photo/name/free text), so activation, AI attach, and step drop-off are computable from a tester's device even before the proxy aggregates them. Pair with the qualitative 'want the next zone' feedback.
findings.spec_change: Add a subsection to 'MVP Beta: Definition & Scope' titled 'Beta instrumentation (on-device)' listing the exact subset of the 14 events captured locally in the beta (setup_complete, zone_started, before_photos_added, sort_plan_requested, step_completed{step}, after_photos_added, coach_review_received, zone_completed{items_released}, audit_action{result}), and add a MUST row to the Build-Ready Feature Backlog: 'On-device loop-milestone event log (privacy-respecting, no PII).'

findings.title: Completion is not gated on a before photo, and the transformation is never shown
findings.observation: A zone is marked done when p.steps.every(Boolean) && p.ap.length>0 (StepPanel) or on after-photo add (PhotoBlock auto-complete). Neither path requires a before photo, so a tester can complete a zone with only an after shot. The before and after galleries are two separate PhotoBlock cards at opposite ends of the ZoneScreen; there is no diptych, no compare, and no completion moment. The activation payoff the whole beta is built to earn (a change you could not un-see) is collected but never plated back to the user.
findings.recommendation: Require at least one before and one after photo to complete a zone, matching the Activation metric's own definition. On completion, present a before/after reveal (the diptych) plus the items-released count and a 'Start next zone' CTA. This is the conversion hinge from one activation to the next.
findings.spec_change: Add an Acceptance Criteria (Functional) bullet: 'A zone cannot be marked complete without at least one before and one after photo.' Add a MUST row to the Build-Ready Feature Backlog: 'Completion reveal: before/after compare view plus items-released and next-zone CTA (in-app, not the deferred share card).'

findings.title: The AI differentiator is unreachable by testers, so attach rate cannot be measured
findings.observation: callAI throws NO_ENDPOINT unless settings.aiEndpoint is set, and the only way to set it is for the user to paste a proxy URL into Settings. No beta tester will do this, so AI attach (spec target: 50 percent of started zones) will read as zero and the headline differentiator, plus its metered COGS, goes untested. The Sort Plan is also gated on before photos existing, which compounds with the previous finding.
