findings.recommendation: Ship the beta with the proxy endpoint pre-configured in the build (read from a bundled config, not user entry) and hide or lock the endpoint field for testers. AI stays optional in code (graceful static-plan fallback is good), but it must be ON by default so the differentiator is actually exercised and sort_plan_requested / coach_review_received fire.
findings.spec_change: In 'The Two Decoupling Workstreams' > '2. AI, through a thin server proxy', add a bullet: 'The beta build ships with the proxy endpoint pre-set; testers do not enter a URL. The Settings endpoint field is hidden or read-only for the beta.' Update the AI attach rate metric note to state it is only valid once the proxy is default-on.

findings.title: No actual time is captured; the 15-to-90-minute core hypothesis is untestable
findings.observation: zoneStats derives 'time invested' as (steps done / 6) * budgeted minutes, so the user-facing stat is the planned budget prorated by steps, not real elapsed time. The app records no session start/end timestamps. The product's central sizing claim, that a zone finishes in 15 to 90 minutes, therefore has no evidence path in the beta, and 'time invested' is a circular restatement of the estimate.
findings.recommendation: Timestamp when a zone runner is first opened and when it completes; capture real on-zone duration (summing sessions if reopened). Use it to validate the 15-to-90-minute design claim and to replace the derived 'time invested' stat with measured time.
findings.spec_change: Add a Success Metrics row: 'Zone duration (actual) | Median wall-clock time from zone_started to zone_completed; validates the 15-to-90-minute design claim | timestamps on zone_started and zone_completed.' Add a note in the MVP scope that 'time invested' is measured, not derived from the budget.

findings.title: The north-star 'items released' conflates discard/donate with relocate
findings.observation: zoneStats computes items as (p.out.d + p.out.t + p.out.r), summing donate, discard, AND relocate, then labels the dashboard card 'items released.' But the spec defines items_released as donate plus discard only (the share-card hook and north-star). Relocate is 'moved elsewhere in the home,' not released from it. The spec's own code-correction row claimed the stat omits relocate; this build over-corrected the other way and now inflates the north-star.
findings.recommendation: Pin one definition: items_released = donate + discard. Track relocate as a separate items_relocated count. Fix zoneStats and the zone_completed event property so the motivational stat and the metric agree.
findings.spec_change: In Success Metrics, tighten the 'Items released' row to 'donate plus discard only; relocate excluded and tracked separately as items_relocated.' In 'What the Code Analysis Confirmed and Corrected,' replace the 'omits relocate' finding with 'items-released stat currently sums all three tallies including relocate; must be donate plus discard only.'

findings.title: The retention engine keeps only a single audit timestamp, losing the loop's history
findings.observation: AuditBlock overwrites p.audit and p.drift on every check, so only the latest audit survives. The authored Sustain guidance says 'two failed audits in a row means the standard is wrong, redesign the zone,' but the app cannot detect two-in-a-row because it stores no history. Dashboard audit-due uses a fixed 7-day cadence for every zone (now-p.audit > 7 days) regardless of traffic, and there is no streak or audit trail. D28 Sustain retention therefore rests on a thin, lossy signal.
findings.recommendation: Store an append-only audit log per zone ([{ts, result}]) instead of overwriting. Surface a hold/drift streak to the user, drive the 'redesign this zone' prompt off two consecutive drifts, and let the audit-due cadence vary by zone traffic (7-day high-traffic, 30-day default).
findings.spec_change: In the Persistence storage schema (prog) and the Backend Data Model zone_progress row, replace 'last_audit_at, drift_flag' with 'audit_log[] of {timestamp, result: holding|drift}'. Add a Success Metrics sub-note that Sustain retention and a new 'Drift rate' health signal are computed from the audit_log, not a single flag.

findings.title: No team-facing six-S drop-off funnel, though step_completed carries the step enum
findings.observation: The step panels are independent collapsibles that do not gate each other, so sessions can stall at any of the six S's. step_completed is specced to carry step (sort..sustain), which is exactly the data needed to see where sessions die, but no team visualization is defined. Success Metrics list scalar targets with no drop-off view, and activation cohorts are described only in prose.
findings.recommendation: Define two named team dashboards for the PM discipline: a six-S completion funnel (zone_started to each step_completed to after_photos to coach_review to zone_completed, showing per-step drop-off) and an activation cohort curve (share of installs reaching zone_completed within 7 days, by weekly cohort). These are the charts that tell us where the loop leaks.
findings.spec_change: Add a subsection to 'Analytics & Instrumentation' titled 'Team dashboards' specifying: (1) Six-S completion funnel keyed on step_completed.step; (2) Activation cohort curve on zone_completed vs app_install; (3) an AI attach and full-loop-AI panel pairing sort_plan_requested and coach_review_received.

findings.title: The SOP-depth signal (substep engagement) is captured but never used or measured
findings.observation: Substeps are the product's moat (3 to 7 authored, technique-encoding steps per activity, stored as p.sb bitmasks), yet checking them affects nothing: not step completion, not the AI review, not any stat, and there is no event for it. As the spec correction notes, the checkboxes look required but do not gate, which confuses testers. So the one behavior that tests the 'system, not a checklist' hypothesis is both invisible in data and ambiguous in the UI.
findings.recommendation: Clarify the affordance (frame substeps as an optional technique guide, not a gate) and capture substep engagement depth per step (how many substeps a tester actually checks). Aggregate it to see whether testers use the SOP depth or just toggle steps done, which directly measures the differentiator's real-world pull.
findings.spec_change: Add an event to the Event taxonomy: 'substep_progress | fires on zone_completed with a per-step count of substeps checked | measures engagement with the SOP depth, the core moat.' Add a Success Metrics row 'SOP depth engagement' and a Build-Ready Feature Backlog note to clarify the substep affordance.

findings.title: User-facing momentum visualization is thin for a habit product
findings.observation: The dashboard shows three scalar stat cards, per-room progress rings, and zone-dot strips. There is no cumulative or time-based view: no zones-over-time momentum, no running items-released milestone, no personal reset story. For a product whose retention depends on felt progress, the in-app momentum picture is minimal, and the strongest emotional asset (accumulated before/after change) is never surfaced across zones.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight momentum view: a cumulative items-released counter with milestone markers and a simple zones-completed-over-time strip. Keep it on-device and privacy-respecting (no photos leave the device). This gives the user a reason to return that does not depend on the deferred notifications.
findings.spec_change: Add a NICE row to the Build-Ready Feature Backlog: 'Momentum view: cumulative items-released with milestones and a zones-over-time strip (on-device).' Note in Success Metrics that items_released is surfaced to the user as a running total, reinforcing the north-star as a motivational stat.
